notes: Tier-1 HTTP only (curl + Magento GraphQL); no block encountered, no Playwright/Claude-in-Chrome needed. robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow. Method: (1) fetched robots.txt/sitemap index (https://www.homesrus.ae/en/sitemap.xml -> 2 sub-sitemaps, ~8900 URLs) and grepped both for christmas/xmas/halloween/diwali/easter/valentine/thanksgiving/new-year/eid/ramadan/festive/holiday/season -> candidates: household/festive-shop/christmas/, eid/furniture/, eid/accessories/, diwali, catalogues-diwali, ramadan2024, ramadan2026, ramadan-dev, new-layout-ramadan-home-page-6981dee8a2d2e. (2) SSR homepage HTML has no live nav (nav is client-rendered) so could not read the mega-menu from HTML alone; instead used the site's Magento GraphQL endpoint (https://www.homesrus.ae/graphql, Store header 'ae_en', root_category_id=2 -- confirmed this is the HRU store, not the same platform's Momstore tenant which resolves on the default/no-Store-header call) to pull the FULL live category tree (categoryList, 3 levels deep from root) as the authoritative site taxonomy -- zero holiday-named nodes appear anywhere in it (Furniture, Household, Just Arrived, Online Exclusives, Bestsellers, HRU All Products, Last Chance, Big Deal, TABBY DAY, Promotions, Homepage, Shop By Collection, etc. -- all merchandising/sale groupings, not seasonal). Only 'Dubai Shopping Festival' matched keyword 'festival' (curations/dsf, 172 products) and was excluded as a commercial retail sale event, not a holiday/cultural festival. (3) Used graphql urlResolver on each sitemap candidate to classify type: diwali, catalogues-diwali, ramadan2026, ramadan2024, ramadan-dev, new-layout-ramadan-home-page-* all resolved to CMS_PAGE (landing/marketing pages, e.g. diwali page titled 'Diwali Landing Page', ramadan2026 titled 'GLAM MY RAMADAN') -> excluded per marketing-page rule, no PLP/product grid on any of them. household/festive-shop/christmas/, eid/furniture/, eid/accessories/ resolved to CATEGORY (genuine PLPs with layered nav, product grid, and Magento 'Items X-Y of N' toolbar counts: Christmas=3, Eid Furniture=42, Eid Accessories=165 -- confirmed against GraphQL categoryList product_count field, which matched). Also found a 4th category candidate 'ramadan/fragrance/' (only as a commented-out href in a homepage mega-menu HTML block) -> graphql urlResolver ID 29218 confirmed CATEGORY type but it 302-redirects to homepage and returns empty from categoryList (disabled) -> excluded as dead/inactive. (4) Cross-checked why Christmas/Eid-Furniture/Eid-Accessories didn't surface in the live categoryList tree walk: their direct parents ('Festive Shop' id 21922 under Household, and 'Eid' id 31109 at root) are themselves disabled/inactive (categoryList by their IDs returns empty, and /en/eid/ and /en/household/festive-shop/ both 302-redirect to the homepage) -- so these are orphaned leftover pages from a past seasonal campaign: still is_active/include_in_menu=1 individually, still real PLPs with real product grids and real counts, still in the public sitemap.xml (crawlable/indexed), but no longer reachable via any live menu path since their grouping parent was switched off after the campaign ended. Included them as genuine seasonal rows per the task's own guidance that sitemap/category-tree discovery counts even without a live nav link, since site-authored taxonomy (URL path + category name + product_count) unambiguously ties them to Eid/Christmas and the product mix supports it (Eid Accessories = gold tiered serving/dessert stands, tea sets -- classic Eid/Ramadan hosting decor; Eid Furniture = sofas/dining sets/TV units, a 'refresh your home for Eid' furniture push; Christmas = candles + a cushion cover under a 'household/festive-shop/christmas' path). Did NOT create an 'Eid'/'Festive Shop' parent grouping row since those parent nodes are disabled and have no live/browsable PLP of their own (302 redirect, no product grid) -- only their live children are listed. (5) Checked Arabic store view (Store header 'ae_ar') -- same root_category_id=2, i.e. identical category structure/IDs, just localized names, so no additional Arabic-only categories exist. (6) No Halloween, Easter, Valentine's Day, Thanksgiving, or New Year category, CMS page, or sitemap URL found anywhere under any keyword variant checked -- genuinely absent from this site's taxonomy, not merely unsearched.
